jobs.title: Embedded Software Lead
jobs.description_text: Meet the team: The Embedded Software team is where the vehicle comes to life. We write and load the firmware that turns raw hardware: sensor kits, custom boards, and main compute, into a reliable, safety-critical machine. Because our software touches nearly every subsystem, we collaborate with engineers from across the company and get hands-on with the newest hardware in the building. As Embedded Software Team Lead, you will lead the engineers responsible for the vehicle’s low-level software platform. You will set technical direction, create the conditions for the team to deliver reliably, and remain close enough to the code and hardware to make sound engineering decisions. You will help take embedded systems from board bring-up and prototype development through integration, validation, and production deployment. This is firmware that carries real passengers. Reliability is a safety requirement, not just a performance goal, and the code your team ships is part of the safety case. Roles & Responsibilities: Lead, mentor, and grow a high-performing embedded software team, including hiring, onboarding, feedback, and career development. Set team priorities, execution plans, and delivery milestones while creating a clear, effective remote operating rhythm. Define and evolve embedded software architecture across MCUs, sensors, custom boards, and main compute. Provide hands-on technical leadership for real-time behavior, fault handling, diagnostics, performance, and maintainability.

jobs.title: Site Safety Manager
jobs.description_text: About the Role: The Site Safety Manager leads the site safety management system for the Glydways Atlanta ATN Pilot Project across construction, integration and testing, commissioning, operations with passenger service, maintenance, modification, recovery, and emergency response. The role reports directly to the Atlanta ATN Pilot Project Director for site delivery and coordination, and functionally to the Glydways Safety Lead within Safety, Quality and Compliance for safety direction, competence, and assurance. Independent of operations, the Site Safety Manager performs site safety audits, restricts access or return to service, stops work or service, and escalates imminent hazards, safety envelope breaches, or incomplete controls. The Site Safety Manager is accountable for occupational safety of everyone at the site, including Glydways personnel, the operating organization, contractors, and visitors, and for the hazards introduced by testing, commissioning, and operation of an automated transit system. This covers OSHA recordkeeping and reporting, hazard communication, lockout/tagout, PPE, work permits, access control, and the controls required wherever construction, testing, and passenger service take place at the same time. The Site Safety Manager understands Operational Limitations and Safety Related Application Conditions (SRACs) established in the Safety Case and owns their site implementation, communication, verification, and enforcement.
